question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Her evaluation will give / me a best indication of / where I stand in the class.
option_1: where I stand in the class.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. me a best indication of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A superlative degree adjective ("best") must be preceded by the definite article "the", not by the indefinite article "a". So "a best indication" is wrong; it must be "the best indication".

◦ Correct: Her evaluation will give me the best indication of where I stand in the class.

• Rule: a/an is used with singular countable nouns in a general sense, while the is used before superlatives (the best, the tallest, the most beautiful) because a superlative points to one unique thing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Her evaluation will give" is correct — subject + future simple "will give".

• Option 1 "where I stand in the class." is a correct noun clause used as the object of "of".

• Option 3 "No error" is wrong because the article mistake clearly exists in the second segment.

NOTE

• Article rules for degrees: positive — "a good indication"; comparative — "a better indication (than)"; superlative — "the best indication". The only common exception is when a superlative is used adverbially without comparison (e.g., "She works best in the morning").

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Know the ropes
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To understand the details.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "know the ropes" means to know/understand the details of how a particular job or activity is done; to be fully familiar with a procedure. (किसी काम की बारीकियाँ जानना)

◦ Example: After a month in the office, the new trainee had begun to know the ropes.

• Origin: The phrase comes from sailing — a sailor had to know which rope controlled which sail before he could be trusted on board.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To break the rules" is unrelated; the relevant idiom would be "bend/break the rules".

• Option 2 "To reveal a secret" corresponds to "let the cat out of the bag" or "spill the beans".

• Option 4 "To fight without any reason" corresponds to "pick a quarrel" or "have a bone to pick".

NOTE

• Related expressions: "show someone the ropes" (to teach a newcomer how things are done), "learn the ropes" (to learn how a job is done), "at the end of one's rope" (to have no patience or strength left).

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

The story shows the importance of self-esteem.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. pride.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Self-esteem" means confidence in one's own worth or abilities; self-respect. Its closest synonym among the options is "pride" (a proper sense of one's own worth and dignity). (आत्म-सम्मान / स्वाभिमान)

◦ Example: Constant criticism can damage a child's self-esteem / pride.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "humility" means modesty and a low view of one's own importance — the opposite sense.

• Option 3 "disgrace" means loss of respect or honour — an antonym of self-esteem.

• Option 4 "shyness" means being timid or reserved with people; it describes social nervousness, not self-worth.

NOTE

• Synonyms of self-esteem: self-respect, self-worth, self-regard, dignity, pride. Antonyms: self-doubt, humility, inferiority complex, disgrace.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

I stare out into the really amazingly dark night.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. obviously.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amazingly" means in a way that causes great surprise or wonder; surprisingly, astonishingly. Its antonym is "obviously", which means in a way that is clear, expected and easily seen — i.e., causing no surprise at all. (आश्चर्यजनक रूप से का विलोम — स्पष्ट रूप से)

◦ Example: Amazingly, he passed without studying. / Obviously, he passed because he studied hard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "shockingly", 2 "unusually" and 3 "astonishingly" all carry the sense of surprise and are therefore synonyms of "amazingly", not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of amazingly: astonishingly, surprisingly, incredibly, remarkably, shockingly. Antonyms: obviously, evidently, predictably, unsurprisingly, expectedly.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Someone who knows a lot about the arts, food, drink, or some other subject
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Connoisseur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "connoisseur" is an expert judge in matters of taste — someone who knows a great deal about the arts, food, wine or some other subject. (पारखी / विशेषज्ञ)

◦ Example: He is a connoisseur of classical music and can identify a raga within seconds.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Pacifist" — a person who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable (शांतिवादी).

• Option 2 "Gourmand" — a person who enjoys eating and often eats too much (a greedy eater); a "gourmet" (not gourmand) is the refined food expert.

• Option 3 "Cynic" — a person who believes people are motivated purely by self-interest (निंदक).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: epicure/gourmet (a person with refined taste in food and drink), aesthete (one who appreciates beauty and art), virtuoso (a person highly skilled in an art, especially music).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Surrender
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Withstand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Surrender" means to give in, yield or stop resisting an enemy or opponent. Its antonym is "withstand", which means to resist successfully; to hold out against pressure or attack. (आत्मसमर्पण करना का विलोम — डटकर सामना करना)

◦ Example: The fort could withstand a long siege; the garrison refused to surrender.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Waive" means to give up a right or claim voluntarily — closer in sense to surrendering, hence not an antonym.

• Option 2 "Stay" means to remain in a place; it does not oppose the idea of yielding.

• Option 3 "Calm" means peaceful/quiet and is unrelated to resistance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of surrender: yield, capitulate, submit, give in, relinquish. Antonyms: withstand, resist, defy, oppose, hold out.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: You are going to figure out everything.
option_2: You are going to figre out everything.
option_3: You are going to figrue out everything.
option_4: You are going to figure out everrything.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. You are going to figure out everything.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt words are "figure" (F-I-G-U-R-E) and "everything" (E-V-E-R-Y-T-H-I-N-G, with a single "r" in "every"). Only Option 1 spells both correctly.

◦ Correct: You are going to figure out everything.

• "Figure out" is a phrasal verb meaning to understand or solve something after thinking about it. (समझ लेना / हल कर लेना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 misspells "figure" as "figre" (the "u" is dropped).

• Option 3 misspells "figure" as "figrue" (letters transposed).

• Option 4 misspells "everything" as "everrything" (a doubled "r").

NOTE

• Commonly confused spellings in SSC papers: figure, familiar, foreign, February, guarantee, occurrence, embarrass, necessary, definitely, separate.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Consecutive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Successive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Consecutive" means following one after the other in unbroken order; in a continuous sequence. Its closest synonym is "successive". (लगातार / क्रमागत)

◦ Example: India won the trophy for three consecutive / successive years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Organized" means arranged in a systematic way — it refers to order of arrangement, not to an unbroken sequence in time.

• Option 3 "Important" means of great significance — unrelated.

• Option 4 "Executive" refers to a senior manager or to the branch of government that executes laws — unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of consecutive: successive, sequential, continuous, uninterrupted, running (e.g., "three days running"). Antonyms: intermittent, sporadic, discontinuous, alternate.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Temparory.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Temparory" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "temporary", meaning lasting for only a limited time; not permanent. (अस्थायी)

◦ Spelling key: TEM + PO + RA + RY (the vowel after "temp" is an o, not an a).

◦ Example: He took a temporary job during the vacation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Molest" (to pester or assault someone), "Reflect" (to throw back light/to think deeply) and "Called" (past tense of call) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Related forms: temporary (adjective), temporarily (adverb), temporariness (noun). Do not confuse with "contemporary" (belonging to the same period / modern).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Can you please pass me that glittery pen black?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. glittery pen black?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The order of adjectives is wrong. In English, an adjective of colour ("black") comes before the noun, not after it, and it follows adjectives of opinion/quality such as "glittery". The correct phrase is "glittery black pen".

◦ Correct: Can you please pass me that glittery black pen?

• The standard order of adjectives is: Determiner – Opinion – Size – Age – Shape – Colour – Origin – Material – Purpose – Noun (remembered as OSASCOMP).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Can you please" is a correct polite request form.

• Option 1 "pass me that" correctly uses the demonstrative "that" with the verb "pass".

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because the adjective-order mistake is clearly present.

NOTE

• Examples of correct adjective order: "a beautiful small old round brown Italian wooden dining table". Colour adjectives never follow the noun they qualify in ordinary usage.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Meteorologists are still ______ to understand sting jets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. working.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses "are still ______", so the blank needs the present participle (V-ing) to complete the present continuous tense — "are still working". The continuous form is required because the effort is ongoing at present. (वैज्ञानिक अब भी प्रयासरत हैं)

◦ Correct: Meteorologists are still working to understand sting jets.

• Structure: am/is/are + V-ing = present continuous.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "on work" is not an English idiom ("at work" is correct, but it cannot take the infinitive "to understand" in this frame).

• Option 3 "worked" (V3/V2) would make it passive/past — "are worked" is wrong here as "work" is intransitive in this sense.

• Option 4 "works" is a finite present simple form and cannot follow the auxiliary "are".

NOTE

• A sting jet is a narrow, extremely strong current of descending air in some intense extratropical cyclones, producing damaging surface winds — a genuine current topic in meteorology.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To scratch one's head
option_1: To think hard in a puzzled way
option_3: To come up with an idea
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To think hard in a puzzled way.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to scratch one's head" means to think hard about something that is confusing or puzzling; to be perplexed. (सिर खुजाना — उलझन में गहराई से सोचना)

◦ Example: The examiners were left scratching their heads over the strange answer sheet.

• It comes from the physical gesture people make when they are puzzled.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To think about good days" would be "take a trip down memory lane".

• Option 3 "To come up with an idea" would be "hit upon an idea" or "a brainwave".

• Option 4 "To lose all the wealth" would be "go to the dogs" or "lose one's shirt".

NOTE

• Similar idioms of confusion: "at sea", "in a fix", "rack one's brains" (to think very hard), "can't make head or tail of it".

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The teacher let the students choose there essay topics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. choose their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed:

◦ The possessive adjective before "essay topics" must be "their" (belonging to them), not "there" (an adverb of place).

◦ After "let + object", the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used — "let the students choose" — so "choose" is retained.

• Correct: The teacher let the students choose their essay topics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "there" is a clear homophone error.

• Option 2 "has choose their" is doubly wrong — "has" does not fit and "has choose" is not a valid verb form (it would be "has chosen").

• Option 3 "chosen there" keeps the wrong word "there" and wrongly uses V3 after "let".

NOTE

• Homophones: their (possessive — their books), there (place — sit there), they're (they are). Causative verbs let / make / have take the bare infinitive: "let him go", "make him work", "have him call me".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Disturbing emotions begin to build into fear, and then ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. terror.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence shows an increasing intensity of emotion: disturbing emotions → fear → and then something even stronger. "Terror" means extreme, overwhelming fear, so it correctly completes the escalation. (आतंक / अत्यधिक भय)

◦ Correct: Disturbing emotions begin to build into fear, and then terror.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "boldness" (courage) and Option 4 "assurance" (confidence) are the opposite of the rising fear described.

• Option 3 "server" (a person who serves / a computer) is contextually meaningless here.

NOTE

• Degrees of fear (weak to strong): apprehension → anxiety → fear → dread → panic → terror. Recognising such intensity ladders helps in fill-in-the-blank and vocabulary questions.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The Tagore House is rehearsing a skit for the school's Annual Day Function.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part "is rehearsing a skit" is already grammatically correct. It is the present continuous tense (is + V-ing) describing an activity going on around the present time, and "a skit" correctly uses the singular article "a" with the singular countable noun "skit".

◦ Correct as printed: The Tagore House is rehearsing a skit for the school's Annual Day Function.

• "The Tagore House" (a school house) is treated as a singular subject, so the singular auxiliary "is" is right.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "has been rehearsing a skits" is wrong — the article "a" cannot go with the plural noun "skits".

• Option 2 "was rehearse a skit" is wrong — after "was" the V-ing form ("rehearsing") or V3 is needed, never the base form.

• Option 3 "is rehearsed an skit" is wrong — the passive is inappropriate here and "an" cannot precede the consonant sound in "skit".

NOTE

• Article rule: use "a" before a consonant sound (a skit, a university) and "an" before a vowel sound (an hour, an MP). Present continuous = am/is/are + V-ing.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

I bowed to him, but he ______ not to see me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. seemed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first clause "I bowed to him" is in the simple past tense, so the second clause joined by "but" must also be in the past tense — "he seemed not to see me". This is the rule of the sequence of tenses.

◦ Correct: I bowed to him, but he seemed not to see me.

• "Seem" is followed by a to-infinitive: "seemed to see / not to see".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "seems" is present simple and clashes with the past "bowed".

• Option 2 "seeming" is a participle and cannot stand alone as the finite verb of the clause.

• Option 3 "seemingly" is an adverb ("apparently") and cannot serve as the verb.

NOTE

• Sequence of tenses: if the principal clause is in the past, the subordinate/coordinate clause is normally also in the past — except for universal truths ("He said that the earth is round").

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A person who does not believe in God
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Atheist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "atheist" is a person who does not believe in the existence of God. (नास्तिक)

◦ Example: Being an atheist, he never visited any place of worship.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Iconoclast" — a person who attacks cherished beliefs or traditional institutions (मूर्तिभंजक).

• Option 3 "Lecher" — a man given to excessive sexual desire; a lustful man.

• Option 4 "Highbrow" — a person who is intellectual and has refined, scholarly tastes.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: theist (one who believes in God), agnostic (one who holds that the existence of God is unknowable), heretic (one who holds beliefs contrary to established religious doctrine), pagan (one holding religious beliefs other than the main world religions).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Their should be Lokpal to check corruption by the bureaucrats and politicians.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Their should be Lokpal to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs the introductory/existential subject "There", not the possessive adjective "Their". "There should be ..." is the correct structure for stating that something ought to exist.

◦ Correct: There should be a Lokpal to check corruption by the bureaucrats and politicians.

• "Their" is a possessive adjective (their car, their duty) and cannot function as the subject of "should be".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "check corruption by" is correct — "check" here means "to control or restrain".

• Option 3 "the bureaucrats and politicians." is correct usage.

• Option 2 "No error" is wrong because the homophone mistake is present.

NOTE

• Homophone trio: there (place / introductory subject), their (possessive), they're (they are). Static GK link: the Lokpal is India's anti-corruption ombudsman set up under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

The Yoruba was (one of the west African city-state culture).
option_2: one of the west African city-state cultures
option_3: one of a west African city-state cultures
option_4: one of the west's African city-state culture
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. one of the west African city-state cultures.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of the + plural noun" is a fixed rule: after "one of the", the noun must be in the plural because we are picking one item out of a group.

◦ Correct: The Yoruba was one of the west African city-state cultures.

• Thus "one of the ... culture" is wrong; it must be "one of the ... cultures".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No substitution required" is wrong because the singular "culture" after "one of the" is ungrammatical.

• Option 3 "one of a west African city-state cultures" wrongly mixes the singular article "a" with the plural noun "cultures".

• Option 4 "one of the west's African city-state culture" keeps the wrong singular "culture" and adds an unnecessary possessive "west's".

NOTE

• Related rule: "One of the + plural noun + singular verb" — "One of the boys is absent." The verb agrees with "one", while the noun after "of the" stays plural.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The researcher team took air ______ from the room every five minutes to rule out the possibility of a virus.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. samples.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "sample" is a small quantity of something taken for testing or analysis. Researchers collect "air samples" to test them in a laboratory — exactly what is required to "rule out the possibility of a virus". (नमूने)

◦ Correct: The researcher team took air samples from the room every five minutes ...

• "Air sample" is the standard scientific collocation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "instances" means examples or occasions, not physical specimens that can be tested.

• Option 2 "slices" refers to thin flat pieces cut from something solid (a slice of bread) — air cannot be sliced.

• Option 4 "droops" means bends or hangs down limply — a verb that makes no sense here.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: take/collect a sample, blood sample, soil sample, random sample, sample size. In statistics, a sample is a subset drawn from a population for study.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

With Halloween only (1) ______ days away, I thought this was a perfect time to talk (2) ______ Zombies. For years, zombies have dominated science (3) ______. These creatures, the walking dead, don't (4) ______ exist, right? Wrong! There are in fact several very real life diseases that could and can make you (5) ______ like a zombie.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a few.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Days" is a plural countable noun, so it takes "a few" (meaning "some, a small number"), not "little/a little", which are used with uncountable nouns.

◦ Correct: With Halloween only a few days away ...

• "A few" carries a positive sense (some, though not many), which suits the friendly tone here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a little" and Option 4 "little" are used with uncountable nouns (a little water, little hope).

• Option 3 "much" is also used with uncountable nouns (much time, much money) and mainly in negatives/questions.

NOTE

• Quantifier rules: few / a few / many / a number of → countable plural nouns; little / a little / much / an amount of → uncountable nouns. "Few" = hardly any (negative); "a few" = some (positive). The same distinction applies to "little" vs "a little".

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

With Halloween only (1) ______ days away, I thought this was a perfect time to talk (2) ______ Zombies. For years, zombies have dominated science (3) ______. These creatures, the walking dead, don't (4) ______ exist, right? Wrong! There are in fact several very real life diseases that could and can make you (5) ______ like a zombie.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. about.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "talk" takes the preposition "about" when we mention the topic of discussion — "talk about zombies" means to discuss zombies. (के बारे में बात करना)

◦ Correct: ... I thought this was a perfect time to talk about Zombies.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "talk of" is possible but far less natural in modern usage and usually means "mention/refer to" in a formal or literary register.

• Option 3 "talk for" would mean speaking on someone's behalf or for a length of time.

• Option 4 "talk by" is not a valid combination in this sense.

NOTE

• Common "talk" collocations: talk about (a topic), talk to/with (a person), talk over (discuss thoroughly), talk into/out of (persuade/dissuade), talk down to (speak condescendingly).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

With Halloween only (1) ______ days away, I thought this was a perfect time to talk (2) ______ Zombies. For years, zombies have dominated science (3) ______. These creatures, the walking dead, don't (4) ______ exist, right? Wrong! There are in fact several very real life diseases that could and can make you (5) ______ like a zombie.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fictions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is about zombies in stories and films, so the required expression is "science fiction" — the genre dealing with imaginary futuristic or scientific themes. The option given in the plural form "fictions" completes "science ______" correctly in meaning. (विज्ञान कथा)

◦ Correct: For years, zombies have dominated science fictions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "friction" means the resistance between two surfaces rubbing together (or a disagreement) — a completely different word.

• Option 2 "freelance" describes self-employed work for different companies — unrelated.

• Option 4 "fickle" is an adjective meaning changeable and unreliable in loyalty — it cannot follow "science" as a noun.

NOTE

• "Science fiction" (sci-fi) is a literary and film genre; note the near-homophones fiction (invented narrative) and friction (rubbing/resistance), which SSC often uses as distractors.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

With Halloween only (1) ______ days away, I thought this was a perfect time to talk (2) ______ Zombies. For years, zombies have dominated science (3) ______. These creatures, the walking dead, don't (4) ______ exist, right? Wrong! There are in fact several very real life diseases that could and can make you (5) ______ like a zombie.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. actually.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Actually" means in reality; in fact. The writer is questioning whether zombies exist in reality, and the very next sentence answers with "Wrong! There are in fact several very real life diseases ..." — the words "in fact" confirm that the blank needs "actually". (वास्तव में)

◦ Correct: These creatures, the walking dead, don't actually exist, right?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "manually" means by hand — meaningless here.

• Option 2 "gladly" means happily/willingly — it does not fit a statement about existence.

• Option 4 "suddenly" means all at once — existence is not a sudden event.

NOTE

• Adverbs of certainty/reality: actually, really, indeed, in fact, truly, genuinely. They are usually placed before the main verb ("don't actually exist") or at the start of a sentence for emphasis.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

With Halloween only (1) ______ days away, I thought this was a perfect time to talk (2) ______ Zombies. For years, zombies have dominated science (3) ______. These creatures, the walking dead, don't (4) ______ exist, right? Wrong! There are in fact several very real life diseases that could and can make you (5) ______ like a zombie.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Act like" means to behave in the manner of someone or something. The diseases can make a person behave like a zombie, so "make you act like a zombie" is the correct expression. (व्यवहार करना)

◦ Correct: ... several very real life diseases that could and can make you act like a zombie.

• Note the causative structure "make + object + bare infinitive" — "make you act" (not "to act").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "state" means to declare something formally — "state like a zombie" is meaningless.

• Option 2 "slake" means to quench or satisfy (thirst) — unrelated.

• Option 3 "run" would only describe movement, not the overall zombie-like behaviour implied.

NOTE

• "Act like" (behave in a manner) vs "act as" (perform the function of): "He acts like a boss" (behaves as though he were one) / "He acts as the treasurer" (holds that role). Causative verbs make, let, have take the bare infinitive.

question: For how many years does the Indian Vice-President hold office?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vice-President of India holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office. (भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति का कार्यकाल — पाँच वर्ष)

• However, he continues to hold office beyond the five-year term until his successor assumes charge, and he is eligible for re-election any number of times.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 63 provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India; Article 64 makes him the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

• He is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament (elected and nominated) by the system of proportional representation with a single transferable vote.

• Minimum age: 35 years; he must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• The Vice-President may resign by writing to the President and may be removed by a resolution passed by an effective majority of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha (Article 67(b)). The President of India also has a five-year term (Article 56).

question: Which among the following was the son of the Mughal emperor Shahjahan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurangzeb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aurangzeb was the son of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal. He won the war of succession (1657–58), imprisoned his father in the Agra Fort and ascended the throne in 1658 with the title Alamgir. (औरंगज़ेब — शाहजहाँ का पुत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shah Jahan's four sons were Dara Shikoh, Shah Shuja, Aurangzeb and Murad Baksh; Aurangzeb defeated all of them.

• Humayun was the son of Babur; Jahangir was the son of Akbar and the father of Shah Jahan.

• Sikandar Lodi belonged to the Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, not to the Mughals.

NOTE

• Mughal succession: Babur (1526) → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb (d. 1707). Shah Jahan's reign is called the Golden Age of Mughal architecture (Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Jama Masjid).

question: Who popularised the 'Pandanallur Style' in Bharatanatyam and received Padma Bhushan in 2004?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alarmel Valli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alarmel Valli is the celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer who popularised the Pandanallur style (bani) of Bharatanatyam and was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2004. (अलार्मेल वल्ली — पंडनल्लूर शैली)

• She trained under the legendary guru Chokkalingam Pillai and his son Subbaraya Pillai of the Pandanallur lineage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni; its major styles (banis) are Pandanallur, Vazhuvoor, Thanjavur, Melattur and Kalakshetra.

• Mallika Sarabhai (daughter of Vikram Sarabhai and Mrinalini Sarabhai) is known for Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi; Kumari Kamala was a noted dancer-actress; Madhuri Dixit is a film actress trained in Kathak.

NOTE

• Other celebrated Bharatanatyam exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra), Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam and Sonal Mansingh.

question: Which type of friction is considered as a self-adjusting force?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Static Friction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Static friction is called a self-adjusting force because it automatically adjusts its magnitude to be equal and opposite to the applied force, up to a maximum value (the limiting friction), so long as the body does not move. (स्थैतिक घर्षण — स्वतः समायोजी बल)

◦ If you push a heavy box with 10 N and it does not move, static friction is exactly 10 N; push with 20 N and it becomes 20 N — until the limiting value is exceeded and the body slides.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kinetic (sliding) friction acts when a body is already sliding and has a nearly constant value (f = μₖN), so it is not self-adjusting.

• Rolling friction acts when a body rolls over a surface and is the smallest of the three, which is why wheels and ball bearings are used.

• There is no such force as "centripetal friction"; centripetal force is the net inward force needed for circular motion.

NOTE

• Order of magnitude: static (limiting) > kinetic > rolling. Friction is independent of the area of contact and depends on the normal reaction (N) and the nature of surfaces (μ). Friction is a necessary evil — it enables walking and braking but wastes energy as heat.

question: Alluri Sitaram Raju was a tribal freedom fighter from state ______ of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alluri Sitarama Raju was a tribal freedom fighter from the Andhra Pradesh region (the Visakhapatnam agency area of the then Madras Presidency). He led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 against the British. (अल्लूरी सीताराम राजू — आंध्र प्रदेश)

• He is popularly called "Manyam Veerudu" (Hero of the Jungle) and was killed by the British in 1924.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Rampa (Manyam) Rebellion was triggered by the Madras Forest Act of 1882, which restricted the tribals' traditional podu (shifting) cultivation and access to forests.

• In 2022, the Government of India celebrated his 125th birth anniversary as part of Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav, and a statue was unveiled at Bhimavaram.

NOTE

• Other major tribal uprisings: Santhal Hul (1855–56) — Sidhu and Kanhu; Munda Ulgulan (1899–1900) — Birsa Munda (Jharkhand); Kol Rebellion (1831); Bhil Revolt; Tana Bhagat Movement.

question: SAI is the apex national sports body of India. What is the full form of SAI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sports Authority of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• SAI stands for the "Sports Authority of India", the apex national sports body of India under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. (भारतीय खेल प्राधिकरण)

• It was set up in 1984 to utilise the infrastructure created for the 1982 Asian Games held in Delhi, and its headquarters is at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, New Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• SAI runs talent-scouting and training schemes such as the National Centres of Excellence (NCOE), Khelo India centres, SAI Training Centres (STC) and the Special Area Games (SAG) scheme.

• It also manages major stadia in Delhi such as the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium and the SPM Swimming Complex.

NOTE

• Related bodies: IOA (Indian Olympic Association), NADA (National Anti-Doping Agency), LNIPE (Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education, Gwalior) and the NSNIS, Patiala (Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports).

question: Who among the following was a Shaka ruler in India (AD 130-150)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudradaman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rudradaman I (c. AD 130–150) was the most famous Shaka (Western Kshatrapa) ruler of India, belonging to the Kardamaka dynasty with his capital at Ujjain. (रुद्रदामन प्रथम — शक शासक)

• He is celebrated for the Junagadh (Girnar) rock inscription of c. AD 150 — the first long inscription in chaste Sanskrit — which records his repair of the Sudarshana Lake, originally built during Chandragupta Maurya's reign and improved by Ashoka.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chashtana was indeed an earlier Western Kshatrapa ruler and the grandfather of Rudradaman, but the specific period AD 130–150 belongs to Rudradaman.

• Bindusara was the Mauryan emperor (son of Chandragupta Maurya, father of Ashoka), not a Shaka.

NOTE

• The Shakas (Scythians) entered India through the north-west in the 1st century BCE. Vikramaditya of Ujjain is traditionally said to have defeated them in 58 BCE, marking the start of the Vikrama Samvat. The Saka Era (78 CE), India's national calendar, is associated with Kanishka.

question: Sam has an income of 9 lakh rupees yearly. Which tax slab (new regime) of India is applicable for him as per the new regime Income Tax Slab Rates FY 2021-22?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the new (concessional) income-tax regime introduced by Section 115BAC for FY 2021-22, the slab of ₹7,50,001 to ₹10,00,000 attracted a tax rate of 15%. Since Sam's annual income is ₹9 lakh, the applicable slab rate is 15%. (नई कर व्यवस्था — 15% स्लैब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• New regime slabs for FY 2021-22: up to ₹2.5 lakh — Nil; ₹2.5–5 lakh — 5%; ₹5–7.5 lakh — 10%; ₹7.5–10 lakh — 15%; ₹10–12.5 lakh — 20%; ₹12.5–15 lakh — 25%; above ₹15 lakh — 30%.

• The new regime offers lower rates but no major exemptions/deductions (such as 80C, 80D, HRA and LTA), whereas the old regime keeps higher rates with deductions.

NOTE

• Income tax is a direct tax levied by the Central Government and administered by the CBDT (Central Board of Direct Taxes) under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. Direct taxes cannot be shifted to another person, unlike indirect taxes such as GST.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution talks about a uniform civil code?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 44.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 44 of the Constitution states that "the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout the territory of India". (अनुच्छेद 44 — समान नागरिक संहिता)

• It falls under Part IV — the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are non-justiciable (not enforceable by any court) but fundamental in the governance of the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 352 — proclamation of National Emergency (war, external aggression or armed rebellion).

• Article 14 — Right to Equality (equality before law and equal protection of the laws).

• Article 370 — the temporary special status of Jammu and Kashmir, abrogated in August 2019.

NOTE

• Goa has long had a common civil code (the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867), and Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to pass a UCC Bill (2024). Other important DPSPs: Article 39A (free legal aid), Article 40 (panchayats), Article 43 (living wage), Article 48A (environment protection).

question: Ustad Bismillah Khan was one of the greatest exponents of the ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shehnai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916–2006) was the greatest exponent of the "Shehnai", a double-reed wind instrument. He is credited with bringing the shehnai — earlier confined to weddings and temple processions — onto the classical concert stage. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खाँ — शहनाई)

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, becoming the third classical musician to receive it.

• He famously played the shehnai from the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, India's first Independence Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Flute (Bansuri) — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh.

• Tabla — Ustad Zakir Hussain, Ustad Alla Rakha, Pandit Kishan Maharaj.

• Sitar — Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tat/Tantu Vadya (string — sitar, sarod, veena), Sushir Vadya (wind — shehnai, flute), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam), Ghan Vadya (solid percussion — manjira, jaltarang).

question: According to census 2011, percentage of Urban population in India is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 31.16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, about 31.16% of India's population lived in urban areas (approximately 37.7 crore people), while about 68.84% lived in rural areas. (जनगणना 2011 — शहरी जनसंख्या 31.16%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 key figures: total population 121.09 crore; sex ratio 943 females per 1000 males; literacy rate 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%); density 382 persons per sq km; decadal growth 17.7%.

• Most urbanised state: Goa (62.2%); most urbanised UT: Delhi (97.5%); least urbanised state: Himachal Pradesh (10%).

• Most populous state: Uttar Pradesh; least populous: Sikkim.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The first synchronous census was held in 1881 under W. C. Plowden. Census 2011 was the 15th national census.

question: The Bhagirathi river originates from Gaumukh Glacier. It meets the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form river ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ganga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhagirathi, which originates from the Gaumukh snout of the Gangotri glacier (Uttarakhand), meets the Alaknanda at Devprayag, and from this confluence the river is known as the Ganga. (देवप्रयाग — भागीरथी + अलकनंदा = गंगा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Panch Prayag (five confluences) of Uttarakhand: Vishnuprayag (Alaknanda + Dhauliganga), Nandprayag (Alaknanda + Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Alaknanda + Pindar), Rudraprayag (Alaknanda + Mandakini) and Devprayag (Alaknanda + Bhagirathi).

• The Ganga is about 2,525 km long — India's longest river — and drains the largest river basin in the country.

• Major left-bank tributaries: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi; right-bank: Yamuna, Son.

NOTE

• The Ganga was declared the National River of India in 2008. In Bangladesh it is called the Padma, and after joining the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) and Meghna it forms the Sundarbans delta, the world's largest delta.

question: Name the brand under which all the fertilizers will be sold under the "One Nation One Fertilizer" scheme launched by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the "One Nation One Fertilizer" scheme (formally the Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Janurvarak Pariyojana — PMBJP), launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2022, all subsidised fertilizers are sold under the single brand name "Bharat". (एक राष्ट्र एक उर्वरक — भारत ब्रांड)

◦ Thus urea is sold as "Bharat Urea", DAP as "Bharat DAP", MOP as "Bharat MOP" and NPK as "Bharat NPK", irrespective of the manufacturing company.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The scheme is implemented by the Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

• Two-thirds of the fertilizer bag now carries the Bharat brand and the PMBJP logo, while the company's own name and logo are limited to one-third of the space.

• Aims: to end brand-based confusion, curb criss-cross movement of fertilizers and reduce high freight subsidy costs.

NOTE

• It was launched along with the PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras (PMKSK) — one-stop shops for seeds, fertilizers, soil testing and farm advisory services.

question: Gangaur is an Indian festival majorly celebrated in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gangaur" is a colourful festival celebrated mainly in Rajasthan (and parts of Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Braj) in the month of Chaitra (March–April). It is dedicated to Gauri (Parvati) and Isar (Shiva). (गणगौर — राजस्थान)

• The name comes from "Gan" (Shiva) + "Gaur" (Gauri/Parvati). Unmarried girls pray for a good husband and married women for the long life and well-being of their husbands.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The festival begins the day after Holi and lasts for 18 days, culminating in grand processions of the images of Gauri, especially in Jaipur, Udaipur, Bikaner and Jodhpur.

• Other important Rajasthani festivals/fairs: Teej, Pushkar Camel Fair, Desert Festival (Jaisalmer), Marwar Festival, Kajli Teej (Bundi).

NOTE

• Festival-state matching for SSC: Bihu — Assam; Onam & Vishu — Kerala; Pongal — Tamil Nadu; Baisakhi — Punjab; Losar — Ladakh/Himachal; Hornbill — Nagaland; Bhagoria — Madhya Pradesh; Gangaur & Teej — Rajasthan.

question: ______ is the division of the cytoplasm of one eukaryotic cell into two daughter cells.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cytokinesis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cytokinesis" is the division of the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell that follows nuclear division and results in two separate daughter cells. (कोशिकाद्रव्य विभाजन)

◦ In animal cells it occurs by the furrowing/constriction of the plasma membrane; in plant cells it occurs by the formation of a cell plate from the centre outwards.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Karyokinesis" is the division of the nucleus, which takes place in four stages — prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase — and normally precedes cytokinesis.

• "Sepsis" is a life-threatening medical condition caused by the body's extreme response to infection; "Genesis" means origin or beginning. Both are unrelated to cell division.

NOTE

• Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells and is used for growth and repair; Meiosis produces four haploid gametes and provides variation. In some cases karyokinesis occurs without cytokinesis, producing multinucleate (coenocytic) cells.

question: The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 belongs to ______ Ministry of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Earth Sciences.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 was introduced and piloted by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). It was passed by Parliament in 2022 and became the Antarctic Act, 2022. (भारतीय अंटार्कटिक विधेयक, 2022 — पृथ्वी विज्ञान मंत्रालय)

• The Act gives effect to India's obligations under the Antarctic Treaty, the Protocol on Environmental Protection (Madrid Protocol) and the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It provides for a Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection, requires a permit for Indian expeditions to Antarctica, prohibits mining and nuclear activity there, and extends Indian jurisdiction over Indian citizens in Antarctica.

• India's Antarctic research stations: Dakshin Gangotri (1983, now decommissioned), Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012). India's Arctic station is Himadri (2008) at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard.

• The nodal agency for polar research is the NCPOR (National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research), Goa, under MoES.

NOTE

• India signed the Antarctic Treaty in 1983 and became a Consultative Party the same year. The Antarctic Treaty (1959, in force 1961) reserves Antarctica for peaceful and scientific purposes.

question: Which city hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beijing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The XXIV Olympic Winter Games (2022) were hosted by Beijing, China, from 4 to 20 February 2022. (बीजिंग — शीतकालीन ओलंपिक 2022)

• Beijing thus became the first city in history to host both the Summer Olympics (2008) and the Winter Olympics (2022).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mascot: Bing Dwen Dwen (a panda); motto: "Together for a Shared Future".

• Norway topped the medal tally with 16 golds. India was represented by a single athlete, the alpine skier Arif Khan.

• Tokyo hosted the Summer Olympics 2020 (held in 2021); Milan-Cortina d'Ampezzo (Italy) will host the Winter Olympics 2026; Melbourne hosted the Summer Olympics in 1956.

NOTE

• Upcoming Olympics: Paris 2024 (Summer), Milan-Cortina 2026 (Winter), Los Angeles 2028 (Summer), Brisbane 2032 (Summer). The Winter Olympics began at Chamonix, France, in 1924.

question: Which Indian state is home to the Buddhist cave temples known as Barabar Caves?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Barabar Caves, situated in the Jehanabad district of Bihar (about 24 km north of Gaya), are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating from the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE). (बराबर की गुफाएँ — बिहार)

• They were excavated during the reigns of Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha Maurya and were donated to the Ajivika sect (with later Buddhist and Jain associations).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Famous caves in the group: Lomas Rishi (noted for its arch-shaped facade imitating wooden architecture), Sudama, Karan Chaupar and Vishwakarma; the nearby Nagarjuni hills contain the Gopika, Vadathika and Vapiya caves.

• The interiors are famous for the Mauryan polish — an extraordinarily smooth, mirror-like finish on the granite walls.

• The caves inspired the "Marabar Caves" in E. M. Forster's novel A Passage to India.

NOTE

• Other important cave sites: Ajanta, Ellora, Elephanta, Karla, Bhaja, Kanheri (Maharashtra), Udayagiri–Khandagiri (Odisha) and Bagh (Madhya Pradesh).

question: Which state is the leading producer of sugar in India, as of May 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of May 2022, Maharashtra was the leading producer of sugar in India, having overtaken Uttar Pradesh in sugar output. (महाराष्ट्र — चीनी उत्पादन में अग्रणी)

• Maharashtra's sugar industry is concentrated in the Ahmednagar, Kolhapur, Solapur, Pune and Satara districts and is dominated by cooperative sugar mills.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Uttar Pradesh remains the largest producer of sugarcane (the raw crop), while Maharashtra has led in sugar (the processed product) in recent seasons owing to higher recovery rates.

• India is the world's largest consumer of sugar and among the largest producers, along with Brazil.

• Sugarcane is a tropical/kharif cash crop needing 21–27°C temperature and 75–150 cm rainfall.

NOTE

• The sugar industry is India's second largest agro-based industry after textiles. Sugarcane by-products: bagasse (fuel/paper), molasses (alcohol/ethanol) and press mud (fertilizer). Ethanol blending with petrol is a major current policy push.

question: Which freedom fighter of India led the famous revolt of 1857 (sepoy mutiny) at Lucknow?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Begum Hazrat Mahal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Begum Hazrat Mahal, the wife of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Awadh, led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow. She proclaimed her young son Birjis Qadr as the ruler of Awadh and organised resistance against the British. (बेगम हज़रत महल — लखनऊ, 1857)

• After the fall of Lucknow she retreated and finally took refuge in Nepal, where she died in 1879.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Centres and leaders of the Revolt of 1857: Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar & General Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb & Tatya Tope; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan; Bihar (Jagdishpur) — Kunwar Singh; Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah.

• The revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, triggered by the greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle; Mangal Pandey at Barrackpore was among the first to rebel.

NOTE

• Consequences: the Government of India Act, 1858 ended Company rule; India came under the direct rule of the British Crown, and Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858) promised non-interference in religious matters. Lord Canning was the last Governor-General and first Viceroy.

question: Pandit Lachhu Maharaj was primarily associated to which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Lachhu Maharaj (1907–1978) was a legendary exponent and choreographer of the "Kathak" classical dance form, belonging to the famous Lucknow gharana of Kathak. (पंडित लच्छू महाराज — कथक)

• He choreographed dance sequences for classic Hindi films such as Mughal-e-Azam, Pakeezah and Mahal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh); the word derives from "Katha" (story) — the kathakars narrated stories through dance. It is noted for fast footwork (tatkar), chakkars (spins) and intricate rhythmic patterns.

• Kathak gharanas: Lucknow (grace and expression — Bindadin Maharaj, Birju Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj), Jaipur (footwork and technique) and Banaras.

• Other Kathak greats: Pandit Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Gopi Krishna.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: The Windvane instrument measures the ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is wind-direction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "wind vane (weather vane)" is the instrument used to measure/indicate the direction of the wind. It consists of a freely rotating arrow-shaped pointer that turns so that its head points into the wind, i.e., towards the direction from which the wind is blowing. (पवन दिशा सूचक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Anemometer — measures wind speed/velocity.

• Hygrometer — measures relative humidity; a wet-and-dry-bulb hygrometer is called a psychrometer.

• Thermometer — measures temperature; Barometer — measures atmospheric pressure; Rain gauge — measures rainfall.

NOTE

• Winds are always named after the direction from which they blow — a "westerly" blows from the west. Other instruments for SSC: seismograph (earthquakes), lactometer (purity of milk), hydrometer (relative density of liquids), altimeter (altitude), odometer (distance travelled).

question: National Family Benefit Scheme was started in August ______ by Government of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS)" was launched on 15 August 1995 as one of the components of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP). (राष्ट्रीय परिवार लाभ योजना — 1995)

• It provides a lump-sum cash assistance to a BPL household on the death of its primary breadwinner (aged 18–59 years). The amount, initially ₹5,000 (₹10,000 for accidental death), was later revised to ₹20,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The NSAP (launched 15 August 1995) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Ministry of Rural Development giving effect to Article 41 of the Constitution (right to public assistance in cases of old age, sickness and disablement).

• NSAP components: IGNOAPS (old-age pension), IGNWPS (widow pension), IGNDPS (disability pension), NFBS (family benefit) and the Annapurna Scheme (free foodgrains to uncovered destitute elderly).

NOTE

• Other schemes launched in 1995: the Mid-Day Meal Scheme (15 August 1995) and the Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana context reforms. NFBS assistance is now generally paid through DBT into the beneficiary's bank account.

question: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in an ecosystem is called ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is stratification.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stratification" is the vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels (strata) in an ecosystem. (स्तरण)

◦ Example: In a forest, trees occupy the top layer (canopy), shrubs the middle layer and herbs/grasses the bottom layer; below that lie the litter and soil layers.

• Stratification allows many species to coexist by reducing direct competition for light and space — an aspect of niche differentiation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Biomagnification" is the increase in the concentration of a non-degradable pollutant (e.g., DDT, mercury) at successively higher trophic levels of a food chain.

• "Coevolution" is the reciprocal evolutionary change in interacting species (e.g., flowers and their pollinators).

• "Decomposition" is the breakdown of complex dead organic matter into inorganic substances by decomposers such as bacteria and fungi.

NOTE

• Steps of decomposition: fragmentation → leaching → catabolism → humification → mineralisation. Other ecosystem attributes: productivity, energy flow, nutrient cycling and stratification. Aquatic ecosystems show stratification too — the littoral, limnetic, profundal and benthic zones.

question: Which famous Indian author of 21st century wrote the novel 'The Immortals of Meluha (Shiva Trilogy)'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amish Tripathi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Immortals of Meluha" (2010) is the first book of the Shiva Trilogy, written by the Indian author Amish Tripathi. (अमीश त्रिपाठी — मेलुहा के मृत्युंजय)

• The Shiva Trilogy comprises The Immortals of Meluha (2010), The Secret of the Nagas (2011) and The Oath of the Vayuputras (2013).

• Durjoy Datta (Of Course I Love You), Ravinder Singh (I Too Had a Love Story) and Shashi Tharoor (The Great Indian Novel, An Era of Darkness, Why I Am a Hindu) are the other listed authors.
